issues.title: Direct malloc/free instead of zmalloc/zfree
issues.description: The rule requires using zmalloc() and zfree() wrappers for memory allocation instead of direct malloc() and free() calls outside of the zmalloc implementation
issues.rule_name: Use zmalloc/zfree Wrappers Instead of Direct malloc/free

issues.title: Off-by-one error causing buffer overflow in extractSlotFromKeysResult
issues.description: The loop condition in extractSlotFromKeysResult uses `j <= keys_result->numkeys` instead of `j < keys_result->numkeys`, causing an off-by-one error. This results in accessing one element beyond the valid range of both the `keys_result->keys` array and the `slot_buffer` array. When numkeys is N, valid indices are 0 to N-1, but the loop accesses index N, leading to out-of-bounds memory access. This can cause crashes, memory corruption, or unpredictable behavior when processing multi-key commands in cluster mode.

issues.title: Incorrect condition causes cross-slot check for keyless commands
issues.description: The condition was changed from `num_keys > 0` to `num_keys >= 0`, which incorrectly includes the case where num_keys equals 0. For keyless commands (num_keys == 0), the slot value may be uninitialized or contain arbitrary data from extractKeysAndSlot. The code will then spuriously check if this uninitialized slot equals CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT, potentially causing false positive cross-slot errors for legitimate keyless commands. This breaks the handling of keyless commands like PING, INFO, or SELECT in cluster mode.

issues.title: Uninitialized slot value for keyless commands due to missing assignment
issues.description: The function extractKeysAndSlot now only sets the slot value when `num_keys > 0`, leaving the slot pointer uninitialized when num_keys is 0 (keyless commands). The caller (preprocessCommand in server.c) expects the slot to always be set by this function. For keyless commands, the slot will contain garbage data or whatever value was previously at that memory location, leading to unpredictable behavior in downstream slot validation logic and potentially causing commands to be incorrectly routed or rejected in cluster mode.

issues.title: Call to extractSlotFromKeysResult without a visible prototype (implicit declaration)
issues.description: src/db.c now calls extractSlotFromKeysResult(), but the diff does not add a function prototype in any included header. In C99+ (as used by Redis), calling a function without a prior declaration results in an implicit function declaration diagnostic, which will fail the build when compiling with -Werror.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
/* Extract slot from the keys result. */
    int slot = extractSlotFromKeysResult(argv, &result);

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14562 - Clean up lookahead-related code

structured_output.summary:
This PR merges two slot-extraction paths into one. `getSlotFromCommand()` now delegates to `extractSlotFromKeysResult()`, the `GETSLOT_NOKEYS`/`GETSLOT_CROSSSLOT` macros are replaced with `INVALID_CLUSTER_SLOT`/`CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT`, and `preprocessCommand()` now detects cross-slot commands through an explicit sentinel instead of guessing from "has keys but slot is invalid". The constant renames, the slot-stats cleanup, the comment fixes and the `getSlotFromCommand` simplification are all sound.

The rewritten `extractSlotFromKeysResult()` is broken, though. Its loop runs `j <= numkeys`, so on every keyed command in cluster mode it reads one entry past the end of `keys` and writes one `int` past the end of a freshly `malloc`'d buffer. That buffer is never read, and it bypasses `zmalloc` too. In practice, single-key commands will likely be misreported as CROSSSLOT, or the server will crash. That blocks the merge. A couple of smaller issues: `extractKeysAndSlot` has a weaker output contract, and one branch condition in `preprocessCommand` is now always true.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The off-by-one loop plus the unused buffer in `extractSlotFromKeysResult()` cause a heap overflow and a read of an uninitialized key entry on the hot command-preprocessing path in cluster mode. That breaks core functionality, so it has to be fixed before merging.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR there were two copies of the same loop. `extractSlotFromKeysResult()` (cluster.c) ran on the lookahead/pipelining path through `extractKeysAndSlot()` → `preprocessCommand()`, and returned INVALID_CLUSTER_SLOT for both 'no keys' and 'cross-slot'; the caller told them apart by checking `num_keys > 0`. `getSlotFromCommand()` (db.c) had its own loop and used the separate GETSLOT_NOKEYS/GETSLOT_CROSSSLOT sentinels for the atomic slot migration (ASM) code in cluster_asm.c.

This PR leaves `extractSlotFromKeysResult()` as the only place that hashes keys to a slot. It now returns three kinds of result: a slot number, INVALID_CLUSTER_SLOT (no keys, or cluster disabled) and the new CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT (-2). `getSlotFromCommand()` becomes a thin wrapper around it. `preprocessCommand()` maps CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT to `CLIENT_READ_CROSS_SLOT` and resets the slot to INVALID before it reaches `c->slot`. The ASM callers switch to the new constants.
steps: Start at `preprocessCommand()` in server.c. It runs for every parsed pending command and calls `extractKeysAndSlot()` to fill `pcmd->keys_result` and `pcmd->slot`.
`extractKeysAndSlot()` in db.c now calls `extractSlotFromKeysResult()` only when `num_keys > 0`. Otherwise it leaves `*slot` alone and relies on the caller having set it beforehand.
`extractSlotFromKeysResult()` in cluster.c is now the single place that computes the slot. It returns a slot, INVALID_CLUSTER_SLOT or CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT.
Back in `preprocessCommand()`, CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT sets `read_error = CLIENT_READ_CROSS_SLOT` and the slot is reset to INVALID so that `c->slot` never holds -2.

`getSlotFromCommand()` in db.c now wraps `getKeysFromCommand()` plus `extractSlotFromKeysResult()`. It's used by `asmFeedMigrationClient()` and `asmModulePropagateBeforeSlotSnapshot()` in cluster_asm.c, which now compare against the new constants.

diagrams.description: Both the lookahead path and the ASM path now go through extractSlotFromKeysResult().

findings.title: Off-by-one loop in extractSlotFromKeysResult reads past keys[] and overflows the heap
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/cluster.c`, `extractSlotFromKeysResult()` (around lines 1103-1127) loops with `j <= keys_result->numkeys`. That reads `keys[numkeys]` (out of bounds or uninitialized) and writes `slot_buffer[numkeys]` past the end of its malloc. Change the loop condition back to `j < keys_result->numkeys`. Also remove the unused `slot_buffer` allocation (see the related finding). Add or keep a cluster-mode test that runs single-key and multi-key same-slot commands (e.g. `MSET {a}x 1 {a}y 2`) and checks they don't fail with CROSSSLOT.

findings.title: Unused per-command malloc'd slot_buffer bypasses zmalloc and is never checked
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/cluster.c`, `extractSlotFromKeysResult()` allocates `slot_buffer` with raw `malloc` (around line 1110), writes to it, and never reads it. Remove the allocation, the writes, and both `free(slot_buffer)` calls, keeping only the `first_slot` tracking. If a temporary buffer is ever really needed, use `zmalloc`/`zfree` per Redis conventions.

findings.title: extractKeysAndSlot no longer always sets its *slot out-parameter
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/db.c`, `extractKeysAndSlot()` (around lines 3185-3205) now sets `*slot` only when `num_keys > 0`, so the out-parameter is left untouched for keyless commands and errors. Add `*slot = INVALID_CLUSTER_SLOT;` before the `if (num_keys > 0)` block so the function always defines its output, regardless of how the caller initialized it.

findings.title: `else if (num_keys >= 0)` is always true after the `< 0` branch
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/server.c` `preprocessCommand()` (around lines 4138-4147), the `else if (num_keys >= 0)` branch is always true because the `num_keys < 0` case returns early. Flatten it to a plain `if (pcmd->slot == CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT) { ... }` after the early return. Behavior stays the same.

findings.title: Explicit CROSSSLOT sentinel plus slot reset is a nice clarification
findings.body:
Before, a cross-slot command was inferred indirectly: "has keys but slot is INVALID". Now `extractSlotFromKeysResult()` returns `CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT` explicitly, and `preprocessCommand()` resets it to `INVALID_CLUSTER_SLOT` before it reaches `c->slot`. That reset matters: `getKeySlot()` checks `current_client->slot >= 0`, and slot-stats paths assert `c->slot >= 0`, so a -2 must never leak through. The PR handles this correctly. Making `getSlotFromCommand()` a wrapper also removes a duplicate copy of the hashing loop.

::code{file="src/server.c" lines="4141-4147"}

findings.title: Behavior change: non-cluster mode now yields INVALID_CLUSTER_SLOT instead of 0
findings.body:
Before, `extractSlotFromKeysResult()` returned `0` when cluster mode was off, so `pcmd->slot`/`c->slot` became 0 for keyed commands. Now they stay at -1. I checked the consumers and this looks safe:
- `getKeySlot()` returns 0 early when `!server.cluster_enabled`.
- `memory_prefetch.c:405` clamps with `pcmd->slot > 0 ? pcmd->slot : 0`.
- The slot-stats checks require `cluster_enabled`.

It's still worth calling out in the PR description, since `c->slot` semantics changed in standalone mode.

::code{file="src/cluster.c" lines="1103-1105"}
